why: RH diagnosis showed the built-in key pose is not a flat six-foot stance (feet spread 0.0166 in z), four legs sit on a joint limit, and holding that pose collapses to COM 0.18 with 29 percent of the weight on non-foot geometry. Every retarget and every controller in this project starts from that pose, so the crouch and the RH slip are inherited, not learned.
change: compute a new standing pose by constrained IK: six material foot points coplanar, total COM height at or above 1.20 native, front/back foot spacing kept close to the built-in pose, joints inside their compiled ranges, and non-foot geometry clear of the floor. The body geometry, joint ranges, actuator gains and all acceptance thresholds are untouched.

acceptance_of_this_step.coplanarity: max |z_i - mean z| over the six feet <= 0.002 native
acceptance_of_this_step.height: total COM z >= 1.20 native at the solved pose
acceptance_of_this_step.clearance: non-foot geometry lowest point >= 0.010 above the solved foot plane
acceptance_of_this_step.ranges: every joint inside its compiled range, at least 0.01 rad away from each bound
acceptance_of_this_step.physical: with the frozen incremental actuator holding the solved pose at rate 0 for 0.4 s, total load share stays within 0.95-1.05 and non-foot load share stays <= 0.02

not_claimed: this is an engineering starting-pose change only; it does not by itself produce accepted walking, and all gates stay exactly as they were
